target: Registry.fs:62 (RCH-09 union labour); registry-components.csv RCH-09; settings.csv registry_mode M1; P3-ASM-MOD049; 11; 14; 16
challenge: Revision 2 charges the M1 human deep review of every charity to Echelon as unfunded shared vendor labour, paid out of an $81 software price. Under licensing (DEC-006) the deep review is a sponsor control: r1 sets a 'sponsor-configured deep-review interval ... a sponsor policy' with reliance snapshots in each sponsor's partition; CNV-GRT-003 allows cross-sponsor evidence 'only as input'; 11 keeps eligibility decisions in the sponsor cell (REV3011); DEC-002 and the brief bar Echelon from becoming an administrator. M1 labour (~$70/account at 2 charities/account) exceeds the $56.70 net price, so the result is structural, not empirical.
evidence: Copy re-run with the M2 vendor cost (sponsor performs the deep review): A3 m120 -$8.70M -> +$21k; break-even 10,963 -> 3,848 accounts; CFO-corrected with M2: payback month 83, peak $2.58M. Partner-book runs: under M1 a larger customer loses more.
proposed_change: Raise an owner decision on who performs and pays for the deep review; base = vendor cost under sponsor-performed review (M2-like); show vendor-performed M1 only as a priced service with matching revenue (sponsor EV-E08 ~$677k at 10k accounts).

challenge: 25% contingency is applied to live run and registry in every live month for 120 months, beyond the AB027 basis ('one-time and pre-revenue cash'), on top of triangular ranges and Monte Carlo draws of the same costs. This double counts uncertainty.
evidence: Copy re-run with contingency on one-time and pre-revenue cost only once live: A3 m120 -$8.70M -> -$5.25M; break-even 10,963 -> 6,833.
proposed_change: Apply contingency to one-time, pre-revenue and the first 12 live months, or show a separate reserve line; keep the ranges as the carrier of run-rate uncertainty.

target: registry-components.csv RCH-09 (2 reviews per union charity-year); P3-ASM-HI029; P3-ASM-HI040
challenge: M1 assumes two 15-minute reviews per charity in use per year, whatever the grant activity. r1: 'an expired deep review MUST hold new approvals', so reviews are demand-driven; a charity granted once a year needs about one review.
evidence: Copy re-run at 1.2 reviews per charity-year (RCH-09 x0.6): A3 m120 -$8.70M -> -$5.20M; break-even 6,282.
proposed_change: Model M1 reviews as distinct 180-day windows with a new approval per charity (grant-frequency distribution; V-3 replay); add as an evidence gap.

target: 11 section 5 M1-M5; UNB-CDD-CIV-008; RR-REQ-X-007-r1; P3-ASM-HI029 low 5 min
challenge: A compliant hybrid that does not rely on OD-CDD-02 is missing: risk-tiered human review (machine-assembled evidence pack and human attestation ~4 min for low risk; 15 min for 20%), performed on demand. A human still performs a comprehensive review at the interval.
evidence: Copy re-run RCH-09 x0.4: A3 -$3.45M, break-even 5,177; combined with demand-driven (x0.24): -$2.05M, break-even 4,538.
proposed_change: Add an M1-tiered mode; put 'does an attested machine-assembled review satisfy r1 comprehensive review' to counsel and the V-9 walkthrough.

target: P3-ASM-MOD041 control_ops_annual; P3-ASM-AB010 basis; P3-ASM-AB013 high; P3-ASM-MOD040
challenge: Control operations ($150-350k) cost two-approver change control that the AB010 maintenance basis already includes ('second maintainer/code approvers ... CNV-PLT-010 contracted approvers'). The adverse case counts the TPSP audit twice (AB013 high includes $50k TPSP; tpsp_annual high $130k). The Nacha base of $75k is unquoted.
evidence: Copy re-run with control operations at a $150k base: A3 m120 -$8.70M -> -$7.58M; break-even 9,937.
proposed_change: Net control operations against AB010; remove TPSP from the AB013 high; obtain an accredited-auditor quote for the TPSP audit.

challenge: The population cap uses all FY2024 sponsors, captive included, times the reachable share. Donation processors count as non-captive (5 of 10 at >=5,291 accounts; 3 of 5 at >=10,963). 'Captive' = national_standard wrongly includes national sponsors that outsource to third-party administrators. The upside is overstated and the denominator is mis-specified.
evidence: Panel counts: >=5,291: 25 all, 15 national, 5 processors, 3 religious, 2 single-issue; model cap 10 vs ~2 (5 x 0.4) excluding national and processors.
proposed_change: Cap on non-captive non-processor sponsors; classify sponsors by platform (own / third-party administrator / unknown) rather than category; rerun the favourable case and the Monte Carlo.

target: Cashflow.fs:139-140 (cap on cumulative signings); sponsor-sizes.csv static FY2024
challenge: The cap counts cumulative signings, so churned customers are never replaced (A3 live decays to 6.1 by m120). The FY2024 panel is held fixed for ten years while sponsors grow into the size bands.
evidence: Copy re-run capping live customers: A3 live m120 6.1 -> 9.4; m120 -$8.70M -> -$7.90M.
proposed_change: Cap live customers plus pipeline; add a panel-growth assumption by size band.

target: Sequences.toStream revenue = accounts x price x (1-share); SEQ-H; P3-ASM-MOD046
challenge: There is no partner-book stream. When a partner's whole book is the customer, the revenue formula holds, but the cap (partners), CAC (per partner), implementation (per sponsor in the book), charities per account and registry overlap all change. Under M1-as-vendor-cost a larger book loses more.
evidence: Copy re-run with 3 books, 1 a year: 20k-account book M1 -$16.8M; M2 +$1.5M (payback 85), implementation x5 -$0.2M; 40k-account book M2 +$10.8M (payback 59), implementation x5 +$9.1M.
proposed_change: Add a partner-book stream with per-sponsor conversion inside the book; state the gate in partner-book accounts.

target: Cashflow.accrue (fractional signings); Sequences.pilotMonth; derivedCostCenter threshold $0; P3-ASM-MOD043; 14 answer 2
challenge: 'Every sequence pauses' is a timing knife edge. A3's pilot comes at month 28 against a month-24 test: fractional signing adds 3 months over a whole first signing (month 25). The clock starts at month 0 only because pre-revenue and control-operations spend begin at month 1, which the recommended gate P3-DEC-MOD003 would defer.
evidence: Copy re-runs: whole first customer -> pilot 25 (still pauses); whole first customer + go-live lag 8 -> pilot 24, A3 passes; kill-sensitivity: cost center at month 6 -> A3 passes.
proposed_change: Sign the first customer as a whole unit; report kill results at lag 8/9 and with the clock at the gate; reword 14 answer 2 as conditional on spend before a named partner.

challenge: Wind-down charges 6 months of full live run when no customer has gone live (any fractional signing triggers it).
evidence: Copy re-run using pre-revenue run when not live: A3 cash at risk $1.81M -> $1.53M.
proposed_change: Wind-down at the pre-revenue run (plus contract exit) until the first go-live.

challenge: The gate 'candidate sponsor at break-even size' is a disguised stop at M1: 10,963 accounts = 14 sponsors (9 national standard, 3 processors, 1 religious, 1 single-issue), about 2 plausible.
evidence: sponsor-sizes.csv counts at >=10,963 accounts.
proposed_change: Restate the threshold after the deep-review allocation decision (~3,000 accounts at M2 vendor cost) and in partner-book accounts.

evidence: UNB-CDD-CIV-008; r1; DEC-002; DEC-006.
proposed_change: Add an allocation decision alongside P3-DEC-MOD004; run V-3/V-9 on the $0-25k ladder before any build.

evidence: Copy re-runs V13: A3 -$1.52M (M1); V15: +$2.00M, payback 83 (M2); V15b: +$1.78M, payback 85 (M5); A from today +$1.02M, payback 101 (M2).
